history.summary: NON-HINDU RECORD (kept with flag): the Golden Pagoda, known locally as Kongmu Kham ('golden pagoda' in Tai Khamti), is a Burmese-style THERAVADA BUDDHIST temple complex, the principal centre of Theravada Buddhism in Arunachal Pradesh - not a Hindu temple. CSV CORRECTION: the row says town Tezu, district Lohit, but the Golden Pagoda stands near Tengapani/Chongkham in NAMSAI district (Namsai district was carved out of Lohit in 2014; old references to Lohit explain the CSV error). The complex sits on a 20-hectare (49-acre) plateau called Noi Chenam. Inaugurated/consecrated on 22 February 2010 after six years of construction by 300+ craftsmen under Myanmar experts, spearheaded by Arunachal politician Chowna Mein (local MLA) with land from the state government; Wikipedia lists the founder as Chow Kon Yein. The main shrine holds a five-tonne bronze Buddha modelled on the Nalanda Kala Buddha, donated from Thailand (1995). The World Tripitaka Foundation is developing Kongmu Kham as India's first international Tripitaka centre. Coordinates from geocoding (27.77241, 95.97562) match Wikipedia's published coordinates (27.7725 N, 95.9749 E).

name: Golden Pagoda
town_description: Namsai is the headquarters of Namsai district in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, on the Tengapani river amid the riverine plains below the Patkai foothills. It is the heartland of the Tai Khamti people who migrated from Upper Myanmar in the 18th century and practise Theravada Buddhism; Namsai district was carved out of Lohit district in 2014.

travel.airport: Dibrugarh Airport (Assam) is the nearest well-connected airport; Tezu Airport (TEI) has limited scheduled flights.
travel.railway: Tinsukia Junction (Assam), about 68 km away, is the nearest major railhead.
travel.road: The pagoda is near Tengapani/Chongkham, about 80 km from Tezu, reached via NH-13/NH-15 through Namsai town; a guesthouse complex on the 20-hectare campus accommodates pilgrims.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March is the pleasantest season; the Kathina festival (usually November) and Sangken (April) are the liveliest times to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Travel guides list 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM daily, closed on certain Buddhist holidays (verify locally). Entry fee may apply.
